name: Superior olivary complex and lateral lemniscus
summary: The first binaural station of the auditory pathway. Axons from the cochlear nuclei cross in the trapezoid body of the caudal pons and converge on the superior olivary complex of both sides, whose neurons compare timing (medial superior olive) and intensity (lateral superior olive) between the two ears to localize sound. Output ascends in the lateral lemniscus to the inferior colliculus. The complex also gives rise to the olivocochlear bundle that tunes the outer hair cells and to the efferent limb of the stapedius reflex through the facial nucleus.

anatomy.location: Ventral tegmentum of the caudal pons, dorsal to the trapezoid body and lateral to the medial lemniscus, just ventromedial to the facial motor nucleus; the lateral lemniscus climbs along the lateral surface of the pontine tegmentum to the inferior colliculus.

function: Sound localization by interaural time and level differences, the acoustic stapedius reflex, and efferent control of the cochlea.

bestView.label: ventral caudal pontine tegmentum behind the trapezoid body
lateral lemniscus on the lateral upper pons

imaging.normalAppearance: Not resolved on routine MRI; localized to the ventral tegmentum of the caudal pons. Pontine lesions here rarely cause deafness because the pathway is already bilateral.

pathology.pathology: Pontine tegmental lesion with hyperacusis or poor localization
pathology.finding: Tegmental infarct or plaque in the caudal pons; hearing is preserved but sound localization and the stapedius reflex are impaired.

imaging.sequenceOfChoice: FLAIR/DWI; audiometry with stapedius reflex testing

lesionEffects.mechanism: Efferent limb of the stapedius reflex

examination: Hearing thresholds are normal; test localization of a sound source with eyes closed
Facial movement and corneal reflex for neighboring structures
pearls: Unilateral deafness never comes from the pons or above
Brainstem auditory evoked potentials map lesions of this pathway wave by wave
